Visit note | 2025-06-14 09:00 AM | Dr. Shirin Akter, Pulmonology | Patient: Popy Miah, 67, female. Mrs. Miah returns for review, reporting that her chest feels tight when she is around dust or cold air, and she continues to have a cough at night. She is a farmer from Rangpur, and her symptoms have been worse since construction dust started near her home. She has no chronic comorbidities. On examination: SpO2 97%, BP 132/71 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 44 kg. Her chest examination reveals scattered wheezes. Assessment: Bronchial asthma. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid dust and smoke, keep her bedroom well aired, and learn the correct inhaler technique. Follow-up in 1 month to check inhaler technique.

Visit note | 2025-06-14 09:00 AM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Shathi Alam, 53, female. Mrs. Alam attends for her first visit, explaining that her abdominal symptoms get worse with stress, she suffers from persistent bloating, and her bowel movements switch between loose stools and hard ones. She works as a construction worker in Old Dhaka, and her complaints worsened after she started this high-pressure job. She has no known comorbidities. On examination: pain score 4/10, BP 122/77 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 60 kg. Her abdomen is soft with mild tenderness in the lower quadrants. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-06-14 09:00 AM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Rubel Awal, 80, male. Mr. Awal presents for his initial evaluation, stating he has been passing urine frequently and has noticed that minor cuts take a long time to heal. He works as a madrasa teacher, and he sought testing after a relative in Jashore received a diabetes diagnosis and advised him to get checked. He denies other systemic complaints and has no major comorbidities. On examination: fasting glucose 7.5 mmol/L, BP 135/70 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, weight 63 kg. Foot examination shows intact peripheral pulses. Assessment: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to reduce rice portions and sweets, walk briskly for 30 minutes five days a week, check his fasting sugar twice weekly, and inspect his feet daily. Follow-up in 3 months with HbA1c.

Visit note | 2025-06-14 09:30 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Masud Gazi, 59, male. Mr. Gazi returns for a follow-up visit, reporting a heavy feeling in his chest that eases with rest within minutes, along with breathlessness on effort and chest tightness when walking fast or climbing stairs. He works as a garment merchandiser and first felt these symptoms while rushing to catch a train in Mohammadpur. He reports no prior chronic illnesses. On examination: BP 133/91 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 64 kg. Heart sounds are dual with no added sounds. Assessment: Stable angina. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid heavy exertion until review, walk 20 minutes daily on flat ground, and stop smoking. Follow-up in 2 weeks with an ECG and fasting lipid profile.

Visit note | 2025-06-14 09:30 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Shahana Howlader, 28, female. Visit note | 2025-06-14 10:00 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Rokeya Sultana, 78, female.
